questions.question: 195 liters of mixture contain the milk and water in the ratio of 7:6, respectively. x liters of water added in the mixture such that the ratio of water to milk becomes 8:7, respectively. Find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk in the initial mixture

\(= \ 195\  \times \ \lbrack\frac{7}{6 + 7}\rbrack\  = \ 105\ liters\)

Quantity of water in the initial mixture

\(195\ –\ 105\  = \ 90\ liters\)

According to the questions,

\(\frac{90 + x}{105}\)= \(\frac{8}{7}\)

630 + 7x = 840

x = 30 liters

Option ‘30 liter’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: 480 liters of a mixture contain milk and water, only, in the ratio of 5:x, respectively. If 20 liters water is added into it, then the ratio of quantity of milk to that of water in the resultant mixture will become 3:2. Find the value of ‘x’.
questions.explanation:
Total quantity of resultant mixture = 480 + 20 = 500

Quantity of milk in resultant mixture = (35) × 500 = 300 litres

Quantity of water in resultant mixture = 500 – 300 = 200 litres

Since the quantity of milk remains constant. So, the quantity of milk in the initial mixture = 300 liters

And, quantity of water in the initial mixture = 480 – 300 = 180 litres

O, the ratio of the quantity of milk and water in the initial mixture = 300:180 = 5:3

So, x = 3

Hence, option e.

questions.question: 132 litres of a mixture (milk + honey) contains milk and honey in the ratio 7:4, respectively. If a certain quantity of the mixture is replaced with 54 litres of honey, then the ratio of quantity of milk to that of honey in the final mixture becomes 2:5. Find the quantity of the mixture that has been replaced.
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk in 132 litres of mixture = \(\frac{7}{11}\) ×132 = 84 litres

Quantity of water in 132 litres of mixture = \(\frac{4}{11}\) ×132 = 48 litres

Let the quantity of Milk and Honey taken out be ‘7x’ liters and ‘4x’ liters, respectively.

According to the question:

\(\frac{84\ –\ 7x}{48\ –\ 4x\  + \ 54}\) = \(\frac{2}{5}\)

Or, 420 – 35x = 96 – 8x + 108

Or, 35x – 8x = 420 – 204

Or, 27x = 216

Or, x = 8

Quantity of mixture that has been replaced = 7x + 4x = 11x = 11×8 = 88 litres

questions.question: In mixture of 90 litres, the ratio of milk to water is 3 : 2. The amount of water to be further added to the mixture so as to make the ratio of the milk to water 2 : 3 will be?
questions.explanation:
In 90 liters of the mixture,

Milk = (35) × 90 = 54 litres

Water = (90 - 54) = 36 litres

Let x litres of water be added

Then, 54(x + 36)=23

⇒ 2x = 90

⇒ x = 45 litres 

∴ The answer is 45 liters.

questions.question: 600 litres of mixture contains 40% water in it and the rest is lime juice. The amount of juice that must be added so that the resulting mixture contains 90% juice is?
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Total mixture = 600 litres
• Water = 40%
• Juice = 60%
• Required juice percentage = 90%

Calculation:
Water = 40% of 600
= (40/100) × 600
= 240 litres

Juice initially = 600 − 240
= 360 litres

Let juice added = x litres

New total mixture = 600 + x
New juice = 360 + x

According to question,

(360 + x) / (600 + x) = 90/100
(360 + x) / (600 + x) = 9/10

10(360 + x) = 9(600 + x)
3600 + 10x = 5400 + 9x

10x − 9x = 5400 − 3600
x = 1800 litres

So, juice to be added = 1800 litres
Hence, option A is correct.

Used Concepts:
• Percentage formula
• Mixture concept
• Ratio equation method

Exam Insight:
In mixture problems, always calculate the fixed quantity first. Here water remains constant at 240 litres. When percentage increases to 90% juice, it means water becomes 10% of new mixture. Using equation method reduces mistakes.

questions.question: In a mixture, the ratio of the alcohol and water is 6:11. When 68 litres mixture is replaced by water, the ratio of alcohol and water becomes 30:90. What is the approximate initial quantity of alcohol?
questions.explanation:
Alcohol in 68 liters =617×68 =24

Water in 68 litres =1117×68 = 44

Let the initial quantity of alcohol and water be 6k and 11k respectively.

6k-2411k-44+68=3090

6k-2411k+24=13

18k - 72 = 11k + 24

7k = 96

k = 13.71

The initial quantity of alcohol = 6k =6×13.71=82.26≈82 L

questions.question: Container A contains 153 kg mixture of zinc and copper in the ratio 4:5. How much copper should be added into container A so as to make the resultant mixture 80% copper?
questions.explanation:
Zinc in the 153 kg mixture =49×153=68 

Copper in the 153 kg mixture =59×153=85

Let x kg copper be added.

(85+x)(153+x)×100=80 (85+x)(153+x)=45425+5x=612+4x x=187

∴ Hence the answer is 187.

questions.question: A mixture contains rosewater and glycerin in the ratio 5 : 3. If 32 liters of mixture is replaced with glycerin, the ratio of rosewater  and glycerin  becomes 13 : 11. Find the quantity of rosewater in the original mixture.
questions.explanation:
Let, initial quantity of rosewater = 5x

And, initial quantity of glycerin = 3x

Then, 32 liters of mixture was taken out

So, Quantity of rosewater in 32 liters mixture =5x5x+3x×32

= 20 liters

And, quantity of glycerin in 32 liters mixture =3x5x+3x×32

= 12 liters

So, Quantity of rosewater left = 5x - 20

And, Quantity of glycerin left = 3x - 12

Again, 32 liters of glycerin is added in the mixture,

So, Quantity of glycerin = 3x - 12 + 32 = 3x + 20

Now, according to the question.

=>5x-203x+20=1311

=> 11(5x - 20) = 13(3x + 20)

=> 55x - 220 = 39x + 260

=> 16x = 480

=> x = 30

So,  initial quantity of glycerin = 3x = 3×(30) = 90 liters

 quantity of rosewater in the original mixture = 5x = 5×(30) = 150 litre

questions.question: A mixture contains honey and syrup in the ratio 7 : 3 respectively. 40 liters of the mixture is replaced by  syrup. Now the ratio of honey and syrup became 21 : 29. Find the quantity of honey in the initial mixture.
questions.explanation:
Let, initial quantity of honey = 7x

And, initial quantity of syrup = 3x

Now, 40 liters of mixture was taken out,

So, quantity of honey in 4 liters mixtures =7x7x+3x×40

= 710×40 = 28 liters

And, quantity of syrup in 40 liters mixture=3x3x+7x×40

= 310×40 = 12 liters

So, quantity of honey left = 7x - 28

And, quantity of syrup left = 3x - 12

Then, 40 liters of syrup is added in mixture,

So, quantity of syrup = 3x - 12 + 40 = 3x + 28

Now, According to question,

=>  7x-283x+28=2129

=> 29(7x - 28) = 21(3x + 28)

=> 203x - 812  = 63x + 588

=> 140x = 1400

=> x = 10

Hence, initial quantity of honey = 7x = 7(10) = 70 liters

questions.question: 500 gram mixture of turmeric and chili powder contains 44% of chili powder. If x gram of turmeric powder is added into the mixture, so that the quantity of turmeric powder in the resultant mixture becomes 60%, find the value of x?
questions.explanation:

As per question;

Ratio of turmeric : chili powder \(= \ 6:4\)

\(\lbrack 280 + x\rbrack:220 = 6:4\)

\( 560 + 2x = 660\)

\( 2x = 100\)

\( x\  = \ 50\ g\)

questions.question: A vessel contains 112 litres of mixture of juice and  water in the ratio of 3:4. If 42 litres of mixture is  taken out from that vessel and then 30 litres of water  added to it, what will be the percentage of juice in the  final mixture?
questions.explanation:
Amount of juice in vessel initially =\(\frac{3}{3 + 4} \times 112 = \ 48\ L\)

And, amount of water in vessel initially =\(\frac{4}{3 + 4} \times 112 = \ 64\ L\)

Amount of juice in 42 litres mixture = \(\frac{3}{3 + 4}\)\(\times\) 42 = 18L

And, amount of water in 42 litres mixture = 42 - 18 = 24L

So, final amount of juice = 48 - 18 = 30L

And, final amount of water = 64-24 + 30 = 70L

Hence, required% = \(\frac{30}{30 + 70} \times 100\  = \ 30\%\)

questions.question: A mixture contains lime juice and water in the ratio 3:2. If it contains 3 liters more lime juice than water, the quantity of lime juice in the mixture is?
questions.explanation:
Let, quantity of water be x and lime juice be x+3.

Given,

\(\frac{x + 3}{x} = \frac{3}{2}\) => x = 6

Hence, Water x= 6 and lime juice = x+3 = 9 liters

questions.question: A very big beaker in the chemistry lab contains a mixture of two acids X and Y in the ratio 5 : 3. When 16 litres of mixture are drawn off and the beaker is filled with Y with the same amount, the ratio of X and Y becomes 5 : 7. How many litres of acid X was contained by the beaker initially?
questions.explanation:
Let, initial quantity of acid X = 5a

And, initial quantity of acid Y = 3a

When, 16 litres of mixture is drawn

Then, quantity of acid X remaining = 5a -  \(\frac{5a}{5a + 3a}\) \(\times\) 16

= 5a - 10

And, quantity of acid Y remaining = 3a - \(\frac{3a}{5a + 3a}\) \(\times\) 16

= 3a - 6

Now, 16 litres of acid Y is added

Then, quantity of mixture Y = 3a - 6 + 16

= 3a + 10

Now, according to question,

=>  \(\frac{5a\  - \ 10}{3a\  + \ 10}\) = \(\frac{5}{7}\)

=> 7(5a - 10) = 5(3a + 10)

=> 35a - 70 = 15a + 50

=> 20a = 120

=> a = 6

So,  initial quantity of acid X = 5a = 5(6) = 30 litres

questions.question: A 10 litre mixture of spirit and water contains spirit and water in the ratio 4 : 1 and 5 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced with pure spirit. This process is done one more time. What is the ratio of spirit to water now?
questions.explanation:
Given the quantity of spirit in the initial mixture = 45×10 = 8 liters

Quantity of water in initial mixture = 15×10 = 2 liters

Then, 5 liters of mixture is removed

So,  Quantity of spirit left = 8 - 4 = 4 litres

And, quantity of water left = 2 - 1 = 1 litres

Then, 4 liters of spirit is added,

So, quantity of spirit = 4 + 5 = 9 litres

So, the ratio of spirit and water = 9: 1

Again, 5 litres of mixture is removed

So, quantity of spirit left = 9 - 4.5   = 4.5 litres

And, quantity of water left = 1 -  0.5 = 0.5 litres

Again 5 litres of spirit is added,

So, quantity of spirit = 4.5 + 5 = 9.5 litres

Thus, ratio of spirit to water = 9.5 : 0.5 = 19:1

questions.question: A 40 litre mixture of soda and water contains soda and water in the ratio 3 : 2. 20 litres of the mixture is removed and replaced with pure soda. This process is done one more time. What is the ratio of soda to water now?
questions.explanation:
As, quantity of mixture = 40 L

So, quantity of soda = 24L

And, quantity of water = 40 – 24 = 16L

Now, 20 L of mixture is drawn out, 12L of soda & 8L of water is drawn out. And same quantity is left

Then, 20L of soda is added, so mixture will have (12+20) 32L soda & 8L water

Again, 20L of mixture is drawn out, 16L of soda & 4 L of water will be drawn out, and same amount would be left.

Now, we again add 20L soda, so mixture will have (16+20) 36L soda & 4L water

Hence, required ratio = 36:4 = 9:1

questions.question: A container contains 192 litres of mixture of water and spirit in the ratio 3:5, respectively. If Raman adds 8 litres of water in the mixture, then what will be the ratio of spirit to water in the final mixture?
questions.explanation:
Quantity of water in initial mixture = \(\frac{3}{\left( 3 + 5 \right)} \times 192 = 72\) L

Quantity of spirit in initial mixture = \(\frac{5}{3 + 5} \times 192 = 120\)

Quantity of water after adding 8 L water = 72 + 8 = 80 L

Hence, required ratio = 120:80 = 3:2

questions.question: A vessel contains 102 liters of mixture of honey and water mixed in the ratio 12 : 5 respectively. ‘y’ liters of the mixture is taken out from the vessel and replaced with 4 liters of water so the ratio of honey to water in the vessel becomes 2 : 1 respectively. Find the value of ‘y’.
questions.explanation:
Quantity of honey in initial mixture = \(\frac{12}{12 + 5} \times 102\) = 72 liters

Quantity of water in initial mixture =  \(\frac{5}{12 + 5} \times 102\) = 30 liters

Then, y liters of mixture is taken out,

So, quantity of honey left = 72 - \(\frac{12}{12 + 5} \times y\)

= 72 - \(\frac{12y}{17}\)

And, quantity of water left = 30 - \(\frac{5}{12 + 5} \times y\)

= 30 - \(\frac{5y}{17}\)

Again, 4 liters of water is added,

So, quantity of water = 30 - \(\frac{5y}{17}\) + 4

Now, According to question,

=> \(\frac{\ 72\  - \ \frac{12y}{17}}{\ 30\  - \ \frac{5y}{17}\  + \ 4}\ \)= \(\frac{2}{1}\)

=> 1(72 - \(\frac{12y}{17}\)) = 2 (30 - \(\frac{5y}{17} + 4\))

=> 72 - \(\frac{12y}{17}\) = 60 - \(\frac{10y}{17}\) +8

=> 4 = \(\frac{12y}{17}\) - \(\frac{10y}{17}\)

=> 4 = \(\frac{2y}{17}\)

=> \(\frac{4\  \times \ 17}{2}\  = \ y\)

=> y = 34 liters

questions.question: 200 liters of a mixture contains 15% water and the rest is Alcohol. The amount of alcohol that must be added so that the resulting mixture contains 87.5% alcohol is?
questions.explanation:
Total mixture = 200 liters

Quantity of water = 15% of 200 = \(\frac{15}{100} \times \ 200 = 30\ liters\)

Quantity of Alcohol = 200 – 30 = 170 liters

Quantity of Alcohol to be mixed = x liters

According to question,\(\frac{170 + x}{200 + x} \times 100 = 87.5\)

x = 40 liters

questions.question: 336 liters of mixture of alcohol and water are in the ratio 4:3 and 84 liters of mixture is taken out and x liters of alcohol is added into the mixture. If the ratio of alcohol and water in the final mixture is 5:3, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation:
Quantity of alcohol = \(\frac{4}{7}\)\(\times\) 336 = 192

Quantity of water = \(\frac{3}{7}\)\(\times\)336 = 144

Since 84 liters of the mixture is removed in the same 4:3 ratio, the alcohol and water removed are:

Alcohol removed = 47×84=48 L

Water removed =  37×84 =36 L

Remaining alcohol and water: 

Alcohol = 192 - 48 = 144 L

Water = 144 - 36 = 108 L

After adding x liters of alcohol, the new alcohol quantity becomes: 144+x

Water remains unchanged at 108 liters.

The new ratio of alcohol : water is given as 5:3, so:

144+x108=53144+x×3=5×108432+3x=5403x=108x=36

The value of x is 36 L.

questions.question: 5 litres are taken out from a bottle full of beer and is then filled with water. This operation is performed two more times. The ratio of the quantity of beer now left in the bottle to that of the water is 8:19. How much beer the bottle hold originally?
questions.explanation:
Let the quantity of beer initially be x l.

Then;

Quantity of beer left after 2 more operations\(\  = \ \lbrack x(1 - \frac{5}{x})^{3}\rbrack\)

\(= > \frac{\lbrack x(1 - \frac{5}{x})^{3}}{x} = \frac{8}{27}\)

\(= > \frac{\lbrack x(1 - \frac{5}{x})^{3}}{x} = (\frac{2}{3})^{3}\)

\(= > 1 - \frac{5}{x} = \frac{2}{3}\)

\(= > x = 15\)

• Final ratio = 2 : 5

Calculation:

After adding water

Water becomes
= 54(a + 1) ÷ (2a + 1) + 30

Final ratio

Multiply denominator

54a ÷ [54(a + 1) + 30(2a + 1)] = 2/5

54a ÷ (54a + 54 + 60a + 30) = 2/5

Cross multiply

270a = 228a + 168

42a = 168

a = 4

Final Answer: 4
Hence, option B is correct.

questions.question: Indian paints mix Red and Yellow in the ratio 4 : 5 in a tank. However, after mixing, the company finds that the resultant shade has less of Red and removes 9 litres of the mixture and adds equivalent quantity of Red. The shade thus obtained has red and yellow in the inverse ratio. How many litres of mixture was there initially in the tank?
questions.explanation:
Let, Initial quantity of red be 4x & yellow be 5x

So, total quantity = 4x + 5x = 9x

Quantity of red in 9 litres mixture = 4 litres

And, quantity of yellow in 9 litres mixture = 9 – 4 = 5 litres

So, total quantity of Red = 4x -4 + 9 = 4x +5

And, quantity of yellow = 5x – 5

According to question,

x = 5

Hence, required quantity = 9x = 9 × 5 = 45 litres

questions.question: 8 kg of metal contains 15th of Tin and the rest is Aluminum. Another 10kg of metal contains 16th of Tin, and the rest is Aluminum. Find the ratio of tin to aluminum. Find the ratio of tin and aluminum in the mixture of these two metals.
questions.explanation: Tin in 8kg metal =15×8=85    & Aluminum in 8kg metal = (1-15 )×8=325  Tin in 10kg metal = 16 ×10=53 & Aluminum in 10kg metal = (1-16 )×10=253So, total Tin in the mixture =85+53 =4915 &  total Aluminum in the mixture = 325+253 =22115Hence, required ratio = 4915:22115  = 49:221

questions.question: An alloy contains Titanium and Tungsten in the ratio 2 : 3  and another alloy contains Titanium and Tungsten in the  ratio 7 : 4. If 2:3 amounts of both the alloys are  melted together, then the ratio of Titanium and Tungsten  the resulting alloy is.
questions.explanation:
Amount of Titanium in 1st alloy =  \(\frac{2}{2 + 3} = \ \frac{2}{5}\)

Amount of Tungsten in 1st alloy = \(\frac{3}{2 + 3} = \frac{3}{5}\)

Amount of Titanium in 2nd alloy = \(\frac{7}{7 + 4} = \ \frac{7}{11}\)

Amount of Tungsten in 2nd alloy = \(\frac{4}{7 + 4} = \frac{4}{11}\)

Let, 2 units of 1st alloy & 3 units of 2nd alloy is mixed

Amount of  Titanium in 3rd alloy = 2\(\times\) \(\frac{2}{5}\) + \(3 \times \frac{7}{11}\) = \(\frac{149}{55}\)

Amount of Tungsten in 3rd alloy =  \(2 \times \frac{3}{5}\) + \(3 \times \frac{4}{11}\) = \(\frac{126}{55}\)

Hence, required ratio = \(\frac{149}{55}\) : \(\frac{126}{55}\) = 149:126

Zinc remained after 48 lit mixture is taken out = (232 − 48) × 58= 115 liter
Required Ratio = (69+18) : (115 + 14) = 29:43

questions.question: 28 kg of an alloy contains 65% copper and rest is zinc. Another 32kg of an alloy contains 40% copper and rest is zinc. If both alloys mix together then find the ratio of copper and zinc in the resultant mixture respectively?
questions.explanation:
Quantity of copper in 28kg alloy = 28 × 0.65 = 18.2

Quantity of zinc in 28kg alloy = 28 - 18.2 = 9.8

Quantity of copper in 32kg alloy = 32 × 0.40 = 12.8

Quantity of zinc in 32kg alloy = 32 - 12.8 = 19.2

Quantity of copper in the resultant mixture = 18.2 + 12.8 = 31

questions.question: 18 L are drawn from a flask full of water and it is then filled with orange juice. 18 L of the resulting mixture are drawn and the flask is again filled with orange juice. The ratio of water to orange juice left in the flask is 8:9. What is the total capacity of the flask?
questions.explanation:
Given Information: 
• Initial liquid is pure water.
• Quantity drawn and replaced (y) = 18 L.
• Number of operations (n) = 2.
• Final ratio of Water to Juice = 8:9.

Calculation:
• The final ratio of Water : Juice is 8:9, so total mixture is 8+9 = 17 parts.
• The fraction of remaining water in the total volume = 8 / (8 + 9) = 8/17.
• Using the formula: (Remaining Water / Total Capacity) = (1 - (y/x))^n.
• 8/17 = (1 - 18/x)^2.
• Taking the square root on both sides: sqrt(8/17) = 1 - 18/x.
• sqrt(8) / sqrt(17) = 1 - 18/x.
• 2.828 / 4.123 = 1 - 18/x.
• 0.686 = 1 - 18/x.
• 18/x = 1 - 0.686 = 0.314.
• x = 18 / 0.314 = 57.32 L (Approximately).

Alternate Method:
• Let Total Capacity = C.
• After first operation, Water left = C - 18.
• After second operation, Water left = (C - 18) * ((C - 18)/C) = (C - 18)^2 / C.
• (C - 18)^2 / C = 8/17 * C.
• (C - 18)^2 = (8/17) * C^2.
• (C - 18) / C = sqrt(8/17) = 0.686.
• C - 18 = 0.686C.
• 0.314C = 18.
• C = 57.32 L.

Used Concepts:
• Mixture and Replacement rule.
• Algebraic ratio application.

Exam Insight:
Always identify the ratio of the remaining original liquid to the total volume first. If the final ratio is Water:Juice = A:B, the fraction of water remaining is A/(A+B).

questions.question: A mixture is composed of 11 parts of pure alcohol and 2 parts of water. If 35 liters of water were added to the mixture then the new mixture will contain twice as much pure alcohol as water, then how many liters of pure alcohol does the original mixture contain?
questions.explanation:
Let the mixture is of ‘13x’ litres

Quantity of alcohol in the mixture = 11x litres

 Quantity of water in the mixture = 2x litres

After adding 35 litres of water, new mixture has (\(2x\  + \ 35\)) part water

After adding 35 Litres of water, the new mixture will contain twice as much pure alcohol as water.

\(\ \frac{11x}{(2x + 35)} = \ \frac{2}{1}\)

\(\Rightarrow \ 4x\  + \ 70\  = \ 11x\)

\(\Rightarrow \ 11x\  - \ 4x\  = \ 70\)

\(\Rightarrow \ 7x\  = \ 70\)

\(\Rightarrow \ x\  = \ 10\ litres\)

∴ Quantity of alcohol in the mixture = 11x = 110 litres

questions.question: A vessel which contains 200 liters of ORS and water solution in the ratio of 3:22. From the vessel 80 liters of mixture is taken out and 9.6 liters of pure ORS solution and pure water, both are added to the mixture. What is the ratio of the quantity of water in the final mixture and the quantity of ORS solution?
questions.explanation:
Given, 80 liters of solution was taken out,

So, remaining solution = 200 – 80 = 120 liters

ORS in remaining solution = 33+22×120 =725 liters

Water in remaining solution = 223+22×120=5285 liters

Adding 9.6 liters of both water & ORS

So, new quantity of ORS = 725+9.6=24 liters

And, new quantity of Water = 5285+9.6=5765 liters

Hence, required ratio = 5765:24=24:5

Required quantity of 2nd mixture = \(\frac{11}{11 + 7}\  \times 72 = 44\ liter\)

questions.question: Three vessels P, Q, and R contains mixture of milk and water. Vessel P contains (2Z + 60) ml milk and 6Y ml water, vessel Q contains (Z + 30) ml milk and (Y + 40) ml water, while vessel R contains Y ml milk and (Z + 20) ml water. When Vessel P poured into vessel Q then amount of milk in vessel Q becomes 50% more than water, if vessel P poured into vessel R than amount of milk and water in vessel R becomes equal. When Q and R mixed in 1:3 respectively than find the % of water in the resultant mixture?
questions.explanation:
According to question,

2Z+60+Z+306Y+Y+40=32

7Y – 2Z = 20…………. (1)

Also,
(2Z + 60 + Y) = (6Y + Z + 20)
5Y – Z = 40……………. (2)
On solving both equations, we get
Value of Y = 20, Z = 60
Ratio of milk and water in Q = 90:60 = 3:2
Ratio of milk and water in R = 20:80 = 1:4
Now,

in Q water=25×100=40%

in R water=45×100=80%

% Of water in resultant mixture  =40%×1+80%×34= 70%

Hence answer is option 2.

questions.question: A mixture P of alcohol and soda contains 75% of alcohol. After 24 liters of soda is added, the alcohol content gets reduced to 50%. If another mixture Q contains the quantity of alcohol equal to the total quantity of mixture P initially such that the ratio of alcohol to soda is 4: 3, then find the quantity of soda in mixture Q.
questions.explanation:
In mixture P ,

Quantity of alcohol = 75% =  75100 =34

And, quantity of soda = 1 - 34 =14

So, ratio of alcohol to soda = 34  : 14 = 3 : 1

Let, quantity of alcohol in mixture P = 3a

And quantity of soda in mixture P = a

Now, 24 liters of soda is added in mixture P,

So, quantity of soda = a + 24

Again, according to question, quantity of alcohol becomes 50%, and soda also 50%, that is, 1:1

=>3aa+24=11

=> 3a = a + 24

=> 2a = 24

=> a = 12

So, initial quantity of alcohol in mixture P = 3a = 3(12) =36 liters

And,  initial quantity of soda in mixture P = a = 12 liters

Now, mixture  Q contains the quantity of alcohol equal to the total quantity of mixture P initially.

So, quantity of alcohol in mixture Q = 3a + a = 4a = 4(12) = 48 liters

And ratio of alcohol and soda in mixture Q = 4:3

So, 4 = 48

=> 1= 12

That is, multiplication factor is 12

Hence, quantity of soda in mixture Q = 3 ×12 = 36 liters

questions.question: A Juicewala has 2 types of mixture of juice with him. In 56 kg of first mixture ratio of juice to impurity is 6 : 2 and in 44 kg of second mixture the ratio of juice to impurity is 3 : 1. If he mixes these two mixture with 17 kg of pure juice in a large container, then find the ratio of juice to impurity in the large container.
questions.explanation:
In 56 kg of first mixture, juice \(= 56 \times \frac{6}{8}\)

= 42 kg and impurity = 56 – 42 = 14 kg

In 44 kg of second mixture, juice \(= 44 \times \frac{3}{4}\)

= 33 kg and impurity = 44 – 33 = 11 kg

In large container quantity of pure juice = 42 + 33 + 17 = 92 kg

In large container quantity of impurity = 14 + 11 = 25 kg

Required ratio = 92 : 25

Therefore, the ratio of juice to impurity in the large container is 92 : 25.

questions.question: A vessel contains a mixture of alcohol and water in the ratio of 4 : 1. 60% of this mixture is taken out and then 4 litres of water is added to the vessel. Further 50% of the mixture is taken out and 6 litres of acid is added. If the initial quantity of the mixture is 200 litres, then find the percentage of water in the resultant mixture.
questions.explanation:
Total amount in the vessel = 200 litres

Quantity of alcohol =\(\frac{4}{4 + 1} \times 200 = 160\)

Quantity of Water =200-160=40

After, 60% of mixture taken out,

Quantity of alcohol left = \(\left( 100 - 60 \right)\%\ of\ 160 = \frac{40}{100} \times 160 = 64\ L\)

Quantity of water left = \(\left( 100 - 60 \right)\%\ of\ 40 = \frac{40}{100} \times 40 = 16\ L\)

Then, 4 litres of water is added,

So, quantity of water = 16 + 4 = 20

Again, 50% of the mixture was taken out

Quantity of alcohol left =\(64\ का\ 100 - 50\% = \frac{50}{100} \times 64 = 32\ L\)

Quantity of water left = (100 – 50)% of 20 =\(\frac{50}{100} \times 20 = 10\ L\)

Then, 6 litres of alcohol is added,

So, quantity of acid = 32 + 6 = 38 litres

Hence, required% =\(\frac{10}{10 + 38} \times 100 = 20.83\%\)

questions.question: Two jars X and Y of equal volume contain Wine and Cranberry juice in the ratio 3 : 2 and 2 : 1 to their brim respectively. Four litres of the solution from jar X and six litres of the solution from jar Y are poured into a big empty jar Z. If the solution in Z occupied 50% of the capacity of Z, what proportion of the volume of jar Z should be the volume of cranberry juice that shall be added so that the ratio of wine and cranberry juice in jar Z becomes equal?
questions.explanation:
Amount of Wine poured in Z = \(4 \times \frac{3}{3 + 2} + 6 \times \frac{2}{2 + 1} = \frac{32}{5}litres\)

Amount of juice poured in Z = \(4 \times \frac{2}{2 + 3} + 6 \times \left( \frac{1}{2 + 1} \right) = \frac{18}{5}litres\)

Given, 10 litres is the 50% capacity of z

So total capacity of Z = 20 litres

To make the quantities of wine and juice same in the vessel Z, quantity of juice to be added =  \(\frac{32}{5} - \frac{18}{5} = \frac{14}{5}\)litres

Hence, required Ratio = \(\frac{\frac{14}{5}}{20} = 7:50\)

% = 750×100=14%

questions.question: A mixture of milk and water comprises 60% milk. First, 30% of the mixture is replaced with water and then the volume of the resultant mixture is increased by 30% by adding only milk. What is approx. percentage of milk in the final mixture?
questions.explanation:
Let total initial quantity of mixture = 100ml

So, quantity of milk = 60% 0f 100 = 60ml

And, quantity of water = 100 – 60 = 40ml

Now, 30% mixture is replaced by water,

So, quantity of milk = (100 – 30) % of 60 =70100×60 =  42ml

And, quantity of water = (100-30) % of 40 + 30% of 100

=  70100×40+30100×100= 58 ml

Again, 30% of the volume is increased by milk,

So increased quantity of milk =30100×100=30ml

Thus, the total quantity of milk = 42 + 30 = 72ml

And total quantity of water = 58ml

Hence, required% =7272+58×100=55.38%

questions.question: A tank contains 1000 liters of water. 100 liters of water is taken out of it and replaced by the same quantity of syrup. This process is repeated one more time. After that 200 liters of the solution is replaced by the same quantity of juice. Find the proportion of syrup, water, and juice in the final mixture respectively ?
questions.explanation:
Given

A tank contains 1000 liters of water.

Calculation Initially Water = 1000 liters

100 liters of water is taken out of it and replaced by the same quantity of syrup

After 1st replacement

Quantity of water = 1000 - 100

And, quantity of syrup = 100

So, Water : Syrup = (1000-100) : (100)

= 900 : 100

= 9 : 1

After 2nd replacement

Quantity of water left,

Water = 900 –  100×99+1

= 900 - 100×910

= 900 - 90

= 810 liters

And, quantity of syrup left

Syrup = 100 – (100×19+1) + 100

= 100 - 10 + 100

= 190 liters

This process is repeated again.

After 3rd replacement

Quantity of water left,

Water = 810 – (200×8101000)

= 810 - (162)

= 648 liters

And, the quantity of syrup left,

Syrup = 190 – (200 ×1901000)

= 190 - 38

= 152 liters

Then again, 200 liters of the solution is replaced by the same quantity of juice, so.

Juice = 200 liters

∴ Required ratio = Syrup : Water : Juice

= 152 : 648 : 200

⇒19 : 81 : 25

questions.question: A person bought a 6-liter bottle of Rum. On the first night, he drank 120ml of its contents and replaced it with water. From the second night onwards, he drank 40 ml more than the previous night and replaced it with water. He continued it till the bottle got empty. What is the total quantity of water used in replacing?
questions.explanation:
On the first night, he drank 120 ml and added 120 ml of water to replace it.

The second night onwards, he drank 40 ml more than the previous night. i.e., 120 + 40 = 160 ml

On third night, 160 + 40 = 200 ml

Capacity of bottle = 6L = 6000 ml

Capacity replaced is –

120 + 160 + 200 + 240 + ...... + 5960 + 6000

In the above expression, 6000 is removed because on the last night, he emptied the bottle without replacement.

So, the expression is –

120 + 160 + 200 + 240 + 280 + .... 5960

This is a arithmetic progression, Tn = a + (n – 1) d

Here, Tn = 5960, a = 120 & d = 40

5960 = 120 + (n – 1) 40

n = 147

The total quantity is calculated by applying the sum formula,

Sn = {a + L} ×  n2

Here, a = 120 , L = 5960 & n = 147

Sn = {120 + 5960} × 1472 = 446880 ml

questions.question: A mixture A of alcohol and water contains 66.66% of alcohol. After 24 litres of mixture A is replaced with water, the alcohol content gets reduced to 50%. If another mixture B contains the same quantity of alcohol as the initial quantity of alcohol in mixture A, and the ratio of alcohol to water in B is 4:3, then find the quantity of water in mixture B.
questions.explanation:
Given Information:
• Initial mixture A contains 66.66% (2/3) alcohol.
• 24 litres of mixture A is replaced by 24 litres of water.
• After replacement, alcohol concentration becomes 50% (1/2).
• Mixture B has alcohol equal to the initial alcohol in A, and the ratio of alcohol to water in B is 4:3.

Calculation:
Let total quantity of mixture A be V litres.
Initial amount of alcohol = (2/3)V.
After removing 24 litres of A, alcohol remaining = (2/3)(V - 24).
Adding 24 litres of water makes the new total volume V.
New percentage of alcohol = [(2/3)(V - 24)] / V = 1/2.
(4/3)(V - 24) = V.
4V - 96 = 3V.
V = 96 litres.
Initial alcohol in A = (2/3) * 96 = 64 litres.
Mixture B has 64 litres of alcohol.
Ratio of alcohol to water in B is 4:3.
4 units = 64 litres, so 1 unit = 16 litres.
Water in B = 3 units = 3 * 16 = 48 litres.

Alternate Method:
Initially A has alcohol and water in ratio 2:1.
After removing 24 litres, remaining mixture A' has ratio 2:1.
Let total volume be V. Removing 24 units reduces total alcohol by (2/3)*24 = 16 units.
New concentration = (Initial Alcohol - 16) / V = 1/2.
Solving for V yields 96 litres, proceed as above.

Used Concepts:
• Replacement of Mixtures.
• Proportionality and Ratios.

Exam Insight:
Remember that in a mixture, removing a portion retains the original ratio of components in the remainder. Use this to quickly calculate the absolute amount of component removed.

questions.question: A milkman orders his servant to mix water in 56 litres of pure milk. With that pure milk the servant first mixes 40 litres of milk and water solution in which the concentration of milk was 60% and then takes out 24 litres from it. Again, he mixes 8 litres of water. What is the concentration of milk in the final mixture?
questions.explanation:
The initial quantity of pure milk = 56 liters

Now, the Concentration of milk in 40 L solution = 60% of 40 = 24L

And concentration of water in 40 L solution = 40 – 24 = 16 L

When 56L of milk & 40 L of solution is mixed,

Quantity of milk in solution =56+24=80 L

And, the quantity of water = 16 L

So, ratio of Milk to water = 80:16 = 5:1

Again 24L of mixture was taken out.

So, the amount of milk taken out =55+1×24=20 l

And, the amount of water taken out = 24 - 20 = 4 L

New quantity of milk = 80 – 20 = 60L

And, new quantity of water = 16 – 4 = 12L

Again, 8 L of water is added, so the quantity of water = 12 + 8 = 20

Hence, the concentration of milk in the final mixture = 60 L

questions.question: 48 gm Rice is mixed in a container, which contains 120 gm pulse. 42 gm mixture from the container is taken out and some quanlity of Rice and pulse are added in the ratio of 2: 1 in the container. If the resulting mixture ratio of pulse and Rice is 11: 6, then what quantity of Rice was added?
questions.explanation:
Total quantity of mixture in container = (48 + 120) = 168 gm

Let 2x gm and x gm of Rice and Pulse added in the container

ATQ—

\(\frac{120 - 42 \times \frac{5}{7} + x}{48 - 42 \times \frac{2}{7} + 2x} = \frac{11}{6}\)

\(\frac{90 + x}{36 + 2x} = \frac{11}{6}\)

\(22x\ –\ 6x\  = \ 540\ –\ 396\ \)

\(16x\  = \ 144\)

\(x\  = \ 9\ gm\)

Quantity of Rice added = 9 × 2 = 18 gm

questions.question: 30 kg of gypsum is mixed with 75 kg of plaster of paris in a container to form a mixture. Then, (p + 5) kg of mixture in container is replaced with 12.5 kg of gypsum and 15 kg of plaster of paris such that the mixture in container now contains \(33(\frac{1}{3}\))% of gypsum. Find the value of ‘p’
questions.explanation:
Ratio of initial quantity of gypsum to plaster of paris in container

= 30:75 = 2:5

Let the quantity of gypsum and plaster of paris withdrawn be 2x kg and 5x kg, respectively

Quantity of gypsum in the final mixture = 30 – 2x + 12.5

= (42.5 – 2x) L

Quantity of plaster of paris in the final mixture = (75 – 5x + 15)

= (90 – 5x) L

Since, \(33\left( \frac{1}{3} \right)\%\) = \(\frac{1}{3}\), therefore

Ratio of gypsum to plaster of paris in the final mixture

= \((\frac{1}{3}\)):{1 – (\(\frac{1}{3}\))} = (\(\frac{1}{3}\)):(\(\frac{2}{3}\)) = 1:2

According to the question,

\(\left\{ \frac{42.5\ –\ 2x}{90\ –\ 5x} \right\} = \frac{1}{2}\)

Or, 85 – 4x = 90 – 5x

Or, x = 5

Therefore, p + 5 = 2x + 5x

Or, p + 5 = 10 + 25

Or, p = 30

questions.question: 456 ml of mixture contains milk and water in the ratio of 12:7, respectively. If ‘a’ ml of mixture is taken out and 285 ml of mixture (milk + water) containing 156\(\frac{1}{4}\)% more water than milk in it, is mixed with the remaining mixture then ratio of milk to water in the resultant mixture becomes 7:12. Find the value of ‘a’.
questions.explanation:
Quantity of milk in 456 ml of mixture = 456 × \(\frac{12}{19}\) = 288 ml

Quantity of water in 456 ml of mixture = 456 – 288 = 168 ml

Let the quantity of milk and water taken out be ‘12x’ ml and ‘7x’, respectively.

156\(\frac{1}{4}\)% = \(\frac{25}{16}\)

Let the quantity of milk in 285 ml of the mixture be ‘b’ ml

So, quantity of water in 285 ml of mixture = (1 + \(\frac{25}{16}\)) × b = \(\frac{41b}{16}\) ml

So, b + \(\frac{41b}{16}\) = 285

Or, b = 80

So, quantity of milk in 285 ml of mixture = 80 ml

So, quantity of water in 285 ml of mixture = 285 – 80 = 205 ml

So, \(\frac{288\ –\ 12x\  + \ 80}{168\ –\ 7x\  + \ 205}\) = \(\frac{7}{12}\)

Or, 4416 – 144x = 2611 – 49x

Or, 95x = 1805

Or, x = 19

So, a = 19x = 19 × 19 = 361 ml

questions.question: 20 liters of a 25% alcohol solution is mixed with ‘y’ liters of a 50% alcohol solution and a resultant solution of 40% alcohol is obtained. Then, ‘2y’ liters of the resultant solution is mixed with 150 liters of a 60% alcohol solution, resulting in a solution of 50% alcohol. What is the percentage difference between ‘y’ and 20?
questions.explanation:
Let's first determine the amount of alcohol in the initial 25% alcohol solution. 25% alcohol means that there are 25 liters of alcohol in 100 liters of the solution.

Therefore, in 20 liters of the solution, there are  = 5 liters of alcohol.

Let's assume that there are 'x' liters of the 50% alcohol solution added to the 20 liters of 25% alcohol solution. Therefore, the total amount of alcohol in the mixture is 5 + 0.5x. The total volume of the mixture is (20 + x) liters.

According to the question, a 40% alcohol solution is obtained after mixing the two solutions. This means that:

= 0.4

Multiplying both sides by (20 + x), we get:

5 + 0.5x = 0.4(20 + x)

Simplifying, we get:

5 + 0.5x = 8 + 0.4x

Subtracting 0.4x from both sides, we get:

0.1x = 3

x = 30

Therefore, 'y' is 30 liters, and the percentage difference between 'y' and 20 is:

=  \(\frac{y - 20}{20} \times 100\) = \(\frac{30 - 20}{20} \times 100\) = 50%

Therefore, 'y' is 50% more than 20.

questions.question:
In a 400 ml mixture of milk and water, milk is _____ % more than that of water. When 160 ml of mixture is removed and replaced with 54 ml water and 36 ml milk, then the ratio of milk and water in the mixture becomes _____ respectively.

I. 50%, 6:5

II. 66.66%, 31:16

III. 200%, 36:19
questions.explanation:
I. 50%, 6:5

Ratio of milk and water in the initial mixture = 3:2

Amount of milk in initial mixture = \(\frac{3}{5}\)× 400 = 240 ml

Amount of water in initial mixture = \(\frac{2}{5}\) × 400 = 160 ml

Ratio of milk and water in new mixture = [240 –\(\frac{3}{5}\)×160 + 36]:[160 – \(\frac{2}{5}\)×160+54] = 180:150 = 6:5

This statement is true.

II. 66.66%, 31:16

Ratio of milk and water in the initial mixture = 5:3

Amount of milk in the initial mixture = \(\frac{5}{8}\) × 400 = 250 ml

Amount of water in initial mixture = \(\frac{3}{8}\) × 400 = 150 ml

Ratio of milk and water in new mixture = [250 – \(\frac{5}{8}\)×160 + 36]: [150 – \(\frac{3}{8}\) × 160 + 54] = 186:144 = 31:24

This statement is not true

III. 200%, 36:19

Ratio of milk and water in the initial mixture = 3:1

Amount of milk in the initial mixture = \(\frac{3}{4}\) × 400 = 300 ml

Amount of water in initial mixture = \(\frac{1}{4}\ \)×400 = 100 ml

Ratio of milk and water in new mixture = [300 – \(\frac{3}{4}\) × 160 + 36]: [100 – \(\frac{1}{4}\) × 160 + 54] = 216:114 = 36:19

This statement is true.

So, Only I and III are true.

questions.question:
Mixture A contains milk and water in the ratio of 5:4 respectively while mixture B contains milk and water in the ratio of 7:9 respectively. If mixture A is mixed with mixture B then total quantity of resultant mixture becomes ____ ml while quantity of water in mixture B is ____ ml more than that in mixture A. Ratio of quantities of milk in mixture A to B is ___ respectively.

The values given in which of the following options will fill the blanks in the same order in which is it given to make the statement true:

I.) 590, 60, 15:14

II.) 756, 99, 20:21

III.) 1080, 100, 10:9

IV.) 1608, 252, 9:7
questions.explanation:
For statement I:

Let quantity of milk and water in mixture A is 5x ml and 4x ml respectively.

Quantity of milk and water in mixture B is 7y ml and 9y ml respectively.

So, 9x + 16y = 590..........................(1)

And, 9y – 4x = 60.........................(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2), we get

x = 30 and y = 20

So, desired ratio = 150:140 = 15:14

So, statement I is true.

For statement II:

Let quantity of milk and water in mixture A is 5x ml and 4x ml respectively.

Quantity of milk and water in mixture B is 7y ml and 9y ml respectively.

So, 9x + 16y = 756..........................(1)

And, 9y – 4x = 99.........................(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2), we get

x = 36 and y = 27

So, desired ratio = 180:189 = 20:21

So, statement II is true.

For statement III:

Let quantity of milk and water in mixture A is 5x ml and 4x ml respectively.

Quantity of milk and water in mixture B is 7y ml and 9y ml respectively.

So, 9x + 16y = 1080..........................(1)

And, 9y – 4x = 100.........................(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2), we get

x = 56 and y = 36

So, desired ratio = 280:252 = 10:9

So, statement III is true.

For statement IV:

Let quantity of milk and water in mixture A is 5x ml and 4x ml respectively.

Quantity of milk and water in mixture B is 7y ml and 9y ml respectively.

So, 9x + 16y = 1608..........................(1)

And, 9y – 4x = 252.........................(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2), we get

x = 72 and y = 60

So, desired ratio = 360:420 = 6:7

So, statement IV is not true.

Hence, option c.

questions.question:
Direction: Study the following data carefully and answer the questions:

Two mixtures A and B contain different quantities of milk and water. Ratio of mixture A to mixture B is 6:5. In mixture A, quantity of milk is ‘x’% and rest is water. In mixture B, quantity of milk is ‘y’% and rest is water. When both the mixtures are mixed together, quantity of milk in the final mixture becomes 63\(\left( \frac{7}{11} \right)\) %.

Note: x + y = 126\(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\)

Which of following is/are true?

P: Quantity of water is equal in both the mixtures.

Q: If cost of mixture A is Rs.32 per L, then cost of pure milk will be Rs. 40 per L.

R: Ratio of milk in mixture A to that of milk in mixture B is 4: 3.
questions.explanation:
Let total quantities of mixture A and mixture B are 6L and 5L respectively.

So, quantity of milk in mixture A = x% of 6L = \(\left( \frac{6x}{100} \right)\ \)L

Quantity of water in mixture A = [6 – \(\left( \frac{6x}{100} \right)\)] L

Quantity of milk in mixture B = y% of 5L = \(\left( \frac{5y}{100} \right)\) L

And quantity of water in mixture B = \(\left\lbrack 5\ –\ \left( \frac{5y}{100} \right) \right\rbrack\) L

Since, when both the mixtures are mixed together, quantity of milk in the final mixture becomes 63\(\left( \frac{7}{11} \right)\) %.

So,

\(\left( \frac{6x}{100} \right)\  + \ \left( \frac{5y}{100} \right)\  = \ (6\  + \ 5)\  \times \ \left( \frac{700}{1100} \right)\)

\(\frac{6x\  + \ 5y}{100}\) = 7

6x + 5y = 700 ------------(1)

Since,

x + y = 126\(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\)

x + y = \(\frac{380}{3}\) ------------(2)

So, by equation (2) × 6 – equation (1):

6x + 6y – 6x – 5y = 760 – 700

y = 60 and x = 66\(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\)

So, ratio of milk to water in mixture A = 66\(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\):33\(\left( \frac{1}{3} \right)\) = 2:1

And ratio of milk to water in mixture B = 60:40 = 3:2

Let quantities of mixtures A and B are ‘6x’ L and ‘5x’ L respectively.

From P:

Quantity of water in mixture A = 6x × \(\left( \frac{1}{3} \right)\) = ‘2x’ L

Quantity of water in mixture B = 5x × \(\left( \frac{2}{5} \right)\) = ‘2x’ L

Since, quantity of water in mixture A = quantity of water in mixture B = ‘2x’ L

So, P is true.

From Q:

Quantity of milk in mixture A = 6x × \(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\) = ‘4x’ L

If the cost of mixture A = Rs.32 per L

Let the cost of pure milk = Rs.’m’ per L

So, \(\frac{4x\  \times \ m}{6x}\) = 32

m = Rs.48 per L

So, Q is not true.

From R:

Quantity of milk in mixture A = 6x × \(\left( \frac{2}{3} \right)\) = ‘4x’ L

Quantity of milk in mixture B = 5x × \(\left( \frac{3}{5} \right)\) = ‘3x’ L

Required ratio = 4x: 3x = 4:3

So, R is true.

Hence, only P and R are true.
